transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I'm here because I just can't seem to keep myself together lately. Since my daughter left for basic training, I feel like I come home to a dead house. 

It's really starting to affect everything. I'm sitting there crying in my truck before my shifts even start. At work, I'm missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and I keep snapping at the younger guys on the floor. When I get home, I don't do much. I've stopped going out on the water, and I haven't been working on my sculpture at all because... I don't know, I just don’t see the point anymore. I just need to figure out how to get a grip on things.
Have you ever felt this way before, like you couldn’t keep yourself together, or is this the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

No, never like this. I mean, sure, I've had hard times before, but... I've always been able to just push through it. Put my head down and work, you know? This is the first time I've ever felt like I'm completely falling apart and can't just shake it off. It's totally new for me.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been about a month. She left a month ago, and... well, I’ve been struggling like this pretty much ever since then.
Before this recent struggle, have you ever had a period of time when you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for more than two weeks in a row?

No, never anything like that. I mean, I've had bad days here and there, just like anybody else, but... not for weeks at a time. I've never felt hopeless or just completely lost interest in my life before this past month. I was always pretty steady.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things almost every day since your daughter left?

I haven't really kept track of every single day, but... yeah, pretty much. I mean, I still drag myself to the shop for work, but I just don't care about anything once I'm there, or when I get home. It just feels like it's been this constant, heavy feeling every day since she moved out.
Besides feeling down and losing interest in things, have you experienced any other changes, like trouble sleeping, feeling tired all the time, or thinking about death or suicide?

No, I haven't really had any of that. I sleep alright, mostly. I mean, I'm usually pretty tired after a shift at the shop just because it's physical work, but it's not any worse than usual. And no, I definitely haven't had any thoughts about dying or suicide or anything like that. It's really just that constant sad feeling I mentioned.
Have you noticed any changes in your thoughts or feelings, like feeling worthless or having trouble concentrating on tasks at work or home?

No, I don't think so. I definitely don't feel worthless or anything like that. And my concentration is... well, it's fine. Working with sheet metal, you really have to pay attention so you don't cut yourself or mess up a measurement, and I haven't had any issues doing the actual work. I just kind of go on autopilot and get it done. So, no, I haven't really had trouble focusing, I just don't care about what I'm doing while I'm there.
Have you found that things you usually enjoy, like going out on the water or working on your sculpture, don’t give you any pleasure anymore?

Yeah, that's exactly it. I haven't been out on the water or touched my sculpture at all. I just don't see the point anymore. Since my daughter left for basic training, I feel like I just come home to a dead house, and I really can't keep myself together. I mean... I'm crying in the truck before my shifts start. And even though I said I can focus enough not to get hurt, I'm actually missing steps on welding jobs I've done for years. I've even been snapping at the younger guys at the shop. It's just... everything feels pointless right now.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually high, extremely energized, or overly irritable where you didn’t need much sleep or felt like you could take on the world?

No, definitely not. I've never had a time like that. I mean, I always need my sleep, especially with the kind of physical work I do. I've never felt... unusually high or super energized like you're saying. It's really just been this heavy, sad feeling lately, nothing at all like being on top of the world.
Has this sadness and loss of interest in things only happened since your daughter left, or have you felt this way even before that time?

No, it's really just been since she left. I was managing okay before she shipped out. I mean, work was fine, life was normal. But this all started within a few weeks of her leaving for basic training. It just hit me all at once after she was gone.
Before this recent time, have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt so down or lost interest in things that it affected your daily life, like work or hobbies?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've had bad days like anyone else, but never anything that lasted weeks or stopped me from doing my work or my hobbies. This... what's happening right now, this is new for me. I've never felt this down before.
Has it been at least two months since you started feeling this way, or has it been less than that?
It's been less than two months. It's really only been about a month since she left for basic training, and that's when all this started. So yeah, just about a month of struggling like this.
Have you had days when you didn't feel this way at all, or has it been pretty much every day since your daughter left?
It's been pretty much every single day. I can't really think of a day where I didn't feel like this... it's just been a constant weight since she left.
Has there been a period in the last month when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks straight without any significant improvement?

Yeah, definitely. Like I was just saying, it's been every single day for about a month now. So it's for sure been at least two weeks straight, and no, it hasn't gotten any better or let up at all. It just stays the same.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating much less or much more than usual?
No, not really. I mean, I eat about the same as I usually do. I haven't noticed any weight loss or weight gain, either. Everything with my appetite seems pretty normal, to be honest.
Have you experienced any other symptoms along with the sadness, such as trouble with sleep, feeling slowed down, or difficulty making decisions?

No, not really. My sleep has been fine, honestly. I haven't had any trouble falling asleep or anything like that. And I don't feel physically slowed down... I still go to work and do my job without any issues. Making decisions hasn't been a problem either. It's really just that constant sad feeling I mentioned.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, where you felt down and lost interest in things almost every day for at least two weeks?
No, I haven't. This is the first time I've ever felt like this for so long. I've never had a stretch of two weeks or more where I was just down and out of it every single day.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this past month when you felt down or lost interest in things almost every day for at least two weeks in a row?

Like I was just saying, no, I really haven't. Before this past month, I've never gone through a time where I felt down or lost interest in things for two weeks straight. This is definitely the first time it's ever been like this.

Looking back at the last month, have you experienced three or more of the following together: feeling down most of the day, losing interest in things, trouble sleeping, feeling tired, changes in appetite, trouble concentrating, or feeling guilty or worthless?

No, definitely not three or more of those. I mean, I have the feeling down part, for sure. But like I said a minute ago, my sleep is completely normal. I'm not having trouble concentrating at work, my appetite is the same as always, and I don't feel worthless or anything like that. So, no, it's really just the sadness.
